checks.invariant: A reviewer-written findings field, the QA report text or a hunt-record string cannot add a Verdict line before the computed one, add a heading or section, or reach a file path or process
checks.result: The computed `Verdict:` line is written at assemble-review.mjs:163, after a table whose Repositories row holds repo/base/branch/head from the findings JSON. In normalize (61-85) those four fields are String() copies and are not made single-line. Finding title, problem, rootCause, fix, strengths, declined and tdd.notes are also unescaped (139-177). The only fields before the real Verdict line are repo, branch, base and head, and head is cut to 12 characters. The coordinator, not a subagent, supplies those four values; the only machine reader of the Verdict line is the agent step in finishing-a-development-branch/SKILL.md:37-49, which reads it as text. Everything the hunt contributes goes through renderReviewSection, which applies oneLine, so the hunt cannot inject structure. Embedded QA images match EMBED (40), which admits `..` inside `artifacts/`; post-review.mjs:99-136 and 233-244 re-check containment, and EMBED is unchanged from dev. The ticket id is validated (236) and the paths go through regularFileProblem/reviewFolderProblem (242-249, 264, 271, 275, 284). No shell or process is reached. The remaining risk is markup and line forgery from reviewer text, listed under hardening.

checks.invariant: Record or tool-lane text (file names from the audited tree, advisory text, finding strings) cannot break out of its table cell, line or heading in SECURITY-REPORT.md or in task-review's section, and cannot forge a Verdict line
checks.result: Every record value passes oneLine (41), which removes \r, \n, U+2028 and U+2029, or cell (42-45), which also escapes `|`. The `|` escape cannot be undone by a trailing or embedded backslash: a pre-existing backslash gives `\\|` and the pipe stays escaped under GFM row splitting, and the template puts a space before each closing pipe. code() (46) swaps backticks for apostrophes. Every list-item and heading builder (findingBlock 558-568, researchLines 571-593, repoBlock 596-671, the front page 675-708) prefixes the value with literal text, so no value can start a block, a heading or a `Verdict:` line. renderReviewSection quotes only the first `Verdict:` line of SECURITY-REPORT.md and passes it through oneLine (712). The repository directory name used in the Cloudflare reports link has `[` and `]` removed in the label and encodeURIComponent in the target (666-668). The preflight accepts only `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` repository names (hunt-preflight.mjs:553). Only inline markup remains: `[](), !, *, <` and autolinks inside a cell are not neutralised (see hardening). The report is written through regularFileProblem (786).

checks.invariant: The verdict says PASS only when every repository the plan selected was hunted to completion in the run being judged, and it never says PASS for an empty, partial or superseded run
checks.result: Fails. latestRun (192-211) takes the highest `run-N` folder and compares it to nothing. loadRun (270-277) builds its repository set from directories that hold a run-metadata.json and silently skips every other directory. The run folder and the repository folders are created before run-metadata.json is written (agents/vulnerability-hunter.md:129 and 137-148). judgeRun (527-545) reaches PASS when `repos` is empty, because the loop adds no part and `run.problems` is empty. In assemble-review.mjs only INCOMPLETE blocks (100, 110), so PASS passes through. The tests cover a missing repo-metadata field and a missing ledger, but no zero-repository run and no missing-repository run; the only mention is the renderReviewSection note at hunt-verdict.mjs:723, which does not change the verdict.

checks.invariant: A record the verdict refuses (tool-lanes.json, an unredacted gitleaks report) must not make rows vanish while a lower-severity result still produces a passing verdict, and the refusal must reach the reader
checks.result: Fails. validLanes (234-244) refuses the whole tool-lanes.json when any single CVE severity is off the four-word scale. loadRun sets toolLanes to null and adds a problem (301-306). analyze then reads `lanes` as [] (390), so the secrets, alerts, notes and every other CVE row of that file are not counted. judgeRun uses `run.problems` only in the last tier (540). Any needs_validation record, OSINT alert or confirmed medium finding gives PASS-WITH-ISSUES first (518-526) and the problem appears in no sentence. renderReviewSection (710-726) never prints run.problems; only the front page does (702-703). The test at hunt-verdict.test.mjs:174-177 makes 'FAIL or PASS-WITH-ISSUES wins over INCOMPLETE' deliberate for run_status; nothing makes it deliberate for refused records. The dependencies lane prompt tells the agent to give the severity 'as the tool states it' in the words critical|high|moderate|low (lane-dependencies.md:29,42), and all lanes share the one tool-lanes.json (agents/vulnerability-hunter.md:159).

candidates.title: An empty or partial hunt run folder, or a newer empty run-N, yields Verdict PASS
candidates.description: The verdict is computed from whatever repository directories hold a run-metadata.json inside the highest-numbered run-N folder. Nothing compares that set with the repositories the preflight selected, with the run number the preflight named, or with the head under review. A run-N folder with no repository directory (the run folder is created before any run-metadata.json exists), or a multi-repository run in which one repository's directory has no run-metadata.json, is judged only on the repositories that remain. With zero repositories judgeRun returns PASS with the sentence 'every repository's run is complete'. task-review treats a hunt PASS as no block, and the SKILL says a hunt that could not run is INCOMPLETE. A hunt that stopped early, or an agent that creates an empty higher-numbered run-N under reviews/<ID>/ (its permitted write area), can therefore turn a FAIL or INCOMPLETE hunt into a PASS in TASK-REVIEW.md.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: latestRun and loadRun define the run and its repository set from the folder tree, and judgeRun treats 'no repository found' as 'nothing wrong' instead of 'nothing was judged', so the verdict has no expected-set check.

trace.description: Picks the highest run-N folder under reviews/<ID>/ with no manifest, no preflight run number and no head or source_ref comparison.

Skips without comment any repository directory that has no run-metadata.json, so a repository that was never completed, or no repository at all, leaves run.repos shorter or empty and run.problems empty.

The INCOMPLETE branch iterates only the loaded repositories; with none, parts stays empty and `verdict = parts.length ? 'INCOMPLETE' : 'PASS'` returns PASS (line 541) with the 'every repository's run is complete' sentence.
Only securityValue === 'INCOMPLETE' blocks; PASS lets the review verdict reach PASS (line 124), and TASK-REVIEW.md (read by finishing-a-development-branch) shows a clean hunt.

evidence.description: Any directory named run-<positive integer> counts; the highest wins, and a mkdir under reviews/<ID>/ is enough.
The run-<N> folder is created in STEP 0b to hold research.json, and repository folders in STEP 1, before run-metadata.json is written, so a stopped hunt leaves exactly the shape that passes.
renderReviewSection prints a note when the run lists no repository, but the verdict itself is not changed, so the strongest source-visible control is a text line.
The tests assert highest-run-wins and the INCOMPLETE cases for a loaded repository; no test covers a run with zero or fewer repositories than planned.
The skill states 'A hunt that could not run is INCOMPLETE in the report', which the empty-run path contradicts.

blockers: The sandbox is unavailable for this run, so judgeRun was not executed on an empty run folder; the PASS comes from reading the source, not from an observed result.
Whether a guarded hunt agent may create a higher-numbered reviews/<ID>/run-N is the guardrail's (unit h1-guardrail), and was not examined here.

validation_plan.local: In a temp project, create reviews/T-1/run-1/ with no repository directory, call loadRun then judgeRun, and expect Verdict INCOMPLETE; repeat with a two-repository plan where one repository directory lacks run-metadata.json. Run assemble-review with the empty run and a passing QA report and expect BLOCKED, not PASS. Suggested change: pass the expected repository names (the preflight's PLAN) into loadRun and add a problem for every missing one and for zero repositories.

candidates.title: A refused tool-lanes.json drops its committed-credential rows, and the refusal is hidden behind PASS-WITH-ISSUES
candidates.description: validLanes refuses the whole tool-lanes.json when one CVE row has a severity off the scale critical/high/moderate/low (medium maps to moderate; 'info', 'none' or 'unknown' do not). The secrets, alerts and notes of every lane in that file then count as zero, the only trace is a loadRun problem, and judgeRun uses problems only in its last tier. If the run has any needs_validation record, an OSINT alert in an unrefused file, or a confirmed medium finding, the verdict is PASS-WITH-ISSUES, not FAIL, the sentence does not mention the problem, and renderReviewSection does not print problems, so TASK-REVIEW.md shows neither the refusal nor the missing secrets. The same demotion hides an unredacted gitleaks report (a committed file) when another issue sets a higher tier.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Records the verdict cannot read are reported as a problem that only matters when nothing else is wrong, and the refusal is whole-file, so rows that were valid are lost with the invalid one.

trace.description: Every CVE of every lane must have a severity on CVE_SCALE or the whole file is refused; the lanes share one file per repository.
On refusal toolLanes stays null and only the problem 'tool-lanes.json is not a lanes object' (a message that names no cause) is added.
`lanes` becomes [] for that repository, so secrets, alerts, notes and cves are all empty and the FAIL condition on committed credentials (line 512) cannot hold.
A needs_validation record or an alert gives PASS-WITH-ISSUES before the branch that reads run.problems (line 540).
The section posted into TASK-REVIEW.md does not render run.problems; only the front page does (lines 702-703), so the refusal is not visible in the task-review report.

evidence.description: The lane agent gives the severity 'as the tool states it' and lists four words, so a tool that states another word produces a refused file; lane-osint.md:41 has the same rule for Dependabot rows.
Every lane block goes into the one tool-lanes.json per repository, so one lane's off-scale row removes the other lanes' secrets.
The tests make 'FAIL or PASS-WITH-ISSUES wins over INCOMPLETE' deliberate for run_status; nothing there covers a refused-record problem combined with a lower-tier issue.
An unredacted gitleaks report is also only a problem (used in the last tier), though the file is committed under reviews/<ID>/.

blockers: The sandbox is unavailable for this run, so judgeRun and loadRun were not executed on a refused tool-lanes.json plus a needs_validation record.
Whether a real audit tool emits a severity word off the four-word scale (for example `info` from npm audit, or an OSV row with no severity) is a fact about the installed tools, not visible in source.

validation_plan.local: Write tool-lanes.json with a secrets lane holding one credential row and a dependencies lane with one CVE of severity 'info', plus one needs_validation record in findings.json; run `hunt-verdict.mjs verdict` and expect FAIL or INCOMPLETE; today it should print PASS-WITH-ISSUES with no mention of the secret or the refusal. Suggested change: validate lane rows individually (or count the secrets of a refused file as an incomplete lane), and make any loadRun problem at least INCOMPLETE in the sentence and the review section whatever the other tier.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner check: run the installed audit tools on a real lockfile and record the severity words in their output.

hardening: Reviewer-written findings text (title, problem, fix, rootCause, strengths, declined, tdd.notes, and the repo/branch/base values in the Repositories row) is written to TASK-REVIEW.md unescaped (assemble-review.mjs:61-85, 139-177, 161). A value with a newline can add a `Verdict:` line or a section heading; the repo/branch/base values stand before the real Verdict line. Apply oneLine to the single-line fields and prefix each line of the free-text fields before posting.

Table cells use only a pipe and newline escape (hunt-verdict.mjs:42-45). File names from the audited tree, advisory text and package names can carry `[text](url)`, `![x](url)`, `<`, `*` and autolink text into the SECURITY-REPORT.md that --post sends to the tracker, which gives a tracking image or a link inside an authoritative comment. Escape or code-span those characters, or put them in a code span.

encodeURIComponent leaves `(`, `)`, `!`, `'` and `*` unescaped (hunt-verdict.mjs:667), so a repository directory name containing `)` breaks the Cloudflare-reports link; the repository-name pattern in the preflight keeps it from happening for names it creates.

judgeRun reads completeness only from the coordinator's own `run_status` (530-533); it never reads the coverage ledger's unit statuses (in_progress, unassigned) and never compares `source_ref` with the head under review, so a stale or half-covered run can be reported as a complete PASS.

In normalizeBlock (369), a research row whose advisory id is already in the CVE table is not counted ('also reported'). If the table records the advisory at a lower severity or as test-only and the research says critical and runtime, the higher claim is dropped. The sentence could keep the higher severity when merging.

Provenance of local checks is verified only in the verdict and front-page commands (hunt-verdict.mjs:776); assemble-review.mjs:254 reads without it. That is deliberate, but the TASK-REVIEW verdict can differ from the front page for a run whose artifact log is absent.
